data.title: Wall Street $500B financing pledge for Nvidia fails to materialize- report
data.description:
A pledge from firms to secure $500B in financing for Nvidia (NVDA) chips, secured by Jensen Huang earlier this year, has failed to materialize, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

Huang, who left the chipmaking giant after a slew of extramarital affairs, got pledges from Apollo Global Management (APO), Blackstone (BX), BlackRock (BLK), Brookfield Asset Management (BAM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and KKR (KKR) in August.

The money would go to Nvidia customers, including OpenAI (OPENAI) and Anthropic (ANT) as well as smaller ones to buy the chips they needed.

However, no capital has been deployed, WSJ said, citing unnamed sources, and investor doubt is creeping in about whether the program will actually pan out, especially with Huang’s exit and the cautious approach of finance head and current interim CEO Colette Kress.

 “We are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees,” Kress said on Tuesday on Nvidia’s earnings call.

data.title: Germany, France lead European gains as UK market trades near six-week low
data.description:
London (UKX) -0.06%, trading near a six-week low after three consecutive sessions of losses, as gains in banking, mining and defence stocks were offset by weakness in consumer-facing stocks.

data.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share, targeting $81B in record-breaking offering
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) has priced its initial public offering (IPO) of Class A common stock at $83 per share above its marketed $70 to $78 range, with the offering comprising 980M shares, up from an earlier plan of 825M shares, reflecting strong investor demand.

Of the total shares on offer, Anthropic is selling 956.35M shares to raise approximately $79.38B in gross proceeds, while certain existing stockholders are selling 23.65M shares for roughly $1.96B.

The company will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by existing stockholders.

At the IPO price, the combined offering raises approximately $81.34B, making it the largest IPO on record and surpassing SpaceX's $75B debut earlier this year.

The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT. The offering is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary closing conditions.

Anthropic has also granted underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 147M shares of Class A common stock.

data.title: 'We gotta bring Jensen back' – Uber co-founder Kalanick weighs in on Nvidia saga
data.description:
Silicon Valley's elite continue to call for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia (NVDA) despite the chipmaker's board affirming that it would not happen.

The latest executive to do so is Travis Kalanick, Uber's (UBER) co-founder and former CEO. "We gotta bring Jensen back," he said at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas on Wednesday.

Kalanick even mentioned showing up at Nvidia's (NVDA) offices to lead employees on a walkout "with a wafer encrusted megaphone."

"Let's fight for what's right and give it a best shot," Kalanick said. "We don't have control of the outcome, but let's fight."

He compared Huang's scandal with his own fight to stay on as Uber's (UBER) CEO amid toxic workplace culture allegations and legal troubles. He stepped down in 2017 after investors demanded his exit.

Huang resigned as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO last week following reports of his extramarital affairs with two women, one of whom U.S. intelligence has alleged is a Chinese spy. 

While Nvidia's (NVDA) chairman Harvey Jones ruled out Huang's reinstatement this week, that hasn't stopped top executives from showing their support for him.

Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk compared Huang's exit to "kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you're on a winning streak," adding that it didn't seem like a smart decision.

"Jensen took one of the earliest big bets on us, we took a big bet on Nvidia," OpenAI (OPENAI) CEO Sam Altman said on Wednesday. "It's hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen."

"I would say Jensen is singular, no question," said Greg Brockman, president, OpenAI (OPENAI). "What Jensen has built there, it clearly is built to last."

Palmer Luckey, co-founder of defense firm Anduril Industries, said nobody could take Huang's place in this critical juncture.

"China wants Jensen out, so I want him in," he added. "There's a reason it's knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out."

Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square, said Nvidia's (NVDA) board was not acting in the best interest of shareholders. "The board's conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history."

More than 200,000 people have signed an online ‌petition demanding Huang's reinstatement pending an independent investigation into his affairs. Signatories include Musk, Kalanick, and Nvidia (NVDA) employees and shareholders.

data.title: Predictiv AI appoints COO Sana Srithas as Interim CEO
data.description:
